solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Something worn in crowd lifted, boy in hat

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word is raised, read from the bottom up
in places the boy inside the hat

parts.note: a beret is a soft flat hat

explanation.surface: A lad wearing a hat is hoisted aloft by a crowd, perhaps at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something worn in crowd' tempts you to read the definition as all of that; the definition stops at 'Something worn', and 'lifted' works on the crowd because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomber jacket is a short zipped jacket, an item of clothing someone wears.

clue.text: New designer left job

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of designer are made into something fresh, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A newly hired designer has already walked out of the post.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resigned is to have quit a position, leaving employment voluntarily.

clue.text: Spot old European currency

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stain or blemish
second meaning: the German ..., replaced by the euro

explanation.definitionFit: A mark is a blemish or stain, and the Deutschmark was Germany's money before the euro.

clue.text: Bit of a smart outfit, fixture in the East End?

parts.note: Bow is a district in the East End of London
a tie is a scheduled sporting fixture, a match

explanation.surface: Asks whether a sports match held in east London is part of formal dress.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of London's East End; a tie, in British sport, is a fixture such as a cup match.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow tie is a neckwear item typically worn with a dinner suit, part of formal attire.

clue.text: Labour man: he's cruel, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately hints that the letters of he's cruel have gone awry and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A union or Labour Party figure is described as sadly cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour man' looks political, but refers to the hero who performed twelve labours in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules is the mythical hero famous for completing twelve tasks, known as labours.

clue.text: Odd characters in cult ain't family!

indicators.note: the odd characters means taking the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of cult ain't

explanation.surface: An outraged insistence that a cult is not a family.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a group of related households, an extended family, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Love huge for Greek character

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone has an enormous crush on a man from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet; character here means a letter.

clue.text: Cooked veal and pork almost coincide

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients mixed and changed, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the last letter of pork is dropped

parts.note: pork is taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Veal and pork prepared together nearly overlap in a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts PORK to POR, which joins VEAL as the fodder for 'Cooked'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlap is to coincide partly, two things sharing some of the same space or time.

clue.text: "Take a risk?", I reply — what if foolish?

indicators.note: foolish suggests the words are muddled up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone responds to a dare by asking what would happen if they did something silly.
explanation.definitionFit: To play with fire is an idiom for doing something dangerous, courting danger.

clue.text: Extraordinary strike by opener for Bangladesh, cut

indicators.note: by means beside, so the opening letter sits next to the rearranged word
the opener for a word is its first letter, here of Bangladesh
extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a remarkable stroke by Bangladesh's opening batsman, a cut shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: an opener is an opening batsman and a cut is a shot, but here cut is the butcher's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef taken from the animal's breast.

clue.text: Tory gains cut by 60 per cent, dance!

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory

indicators.note: sixty per cent of a five-letter word is three letters, so only the first two of gains survive

parts.note: gains is taken as written before it is cut

explanation.surface: Celebrating Conservative gains being slashed by well over half by dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, abbreviated CON. Cutting three of five letters leaves GA.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American dance performed in a line of people.

clue.text: Jog one's memory — as would campanologist?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sound familiar, prompting recall
second meaning: a campanologist is a bell-ringer, who literally does this

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sound familiar, and literally it describes what a bell-ringer does with a bell.

clue.text: Lively dancing in ad entertains friend

indicators.note: entertains means holds as a guest, so one part goes inside the other
dancing means the letters of in ad move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is energetically dancing in an advert featuring a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' turns IN AD into ANID, which 'entertains' MATE to give ANI-MATE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated means full of life and energy, spirited.

clue.text: Gossip just as wicked, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Gossip is just as wicked as the thing it spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: To jaw is informal for chatting at length, chatter or idle talk.

clue.text: Heartless judge with a bad feeling of resentment

indicators.note: heartless means the inside of the word judge is removed, leaving only its ends

parts.note: judge taken as written before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A cruel judge harbours bitter feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes UDG from JUDGE, leaving JE.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy is a resentful envy of someone else's success or advantages.

clue.text: Charity some Canadians backed

indicators.note: backed means the run of letters is turned to read backwards
some indicates that only part of the word Canadians is used

explanation.surface: A charity supported by some people from Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'Canadians' sits DIA; 'backed' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid is help given to those in need, as charity provides.

clue.text: Never stopping, vessel guzzled by ancient drunk

indicators.note: guzzled by means swallowed, held inside the other letters
drunk suggests the word ancient is staggering about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: An old drunkard swallows down a whole vessel of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, for steamship, is the standard crossword vessel; 'drunk' rearranges the letters of 'ancient' around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means continuing without pause or interruption.

clue.text: Spaniard initially inspired by old measure, Picasso say

indicators.note: inspired by means breathed in, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: a cubit is an ancient measure of length, roughly a forearm

indicators.note: initially indicates the first letter of Spaniard

explanation.surface: A Spanish painter is inspired by an ancient unit, and Picasso is the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso co-founded Cubism, so he is an example of a Cubist painter.

clue.text: Curry scoffed by Jack or Margaret

indicators.note: scoffed by means eaten up by, so the letters sit concealed inside Jack or Margaret

explanation.surface: Either Jack or Margaret wolfed down the curry.
explanation.definitionFit: A korma is a mild, creamy Indian dish, a type of curry.

clue.text: Coach with roof off, wet

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, which is taken away

explanation.surface: An open-topped coach leaves passengers soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a vehicle, which suits 'roof', but it is the verb TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet can be a noun meaning rainy weather, as in 'out in the wet'.

clue.text: Go away — as would busy workers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rude instruction to leave
second meaning: busy workers are bees, which buzz as they fly off

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for a dismissive command to leave, and also literally describes bees flying away humming.

clue.text: Queen in Australia rising for nothing

indicators.note: in places the Queen inside the other letters
rising in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch's popularity in Australia climbs from nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is the number meaning none at all, nought.

clue.text: Muscle priest strained carrying lid of casket

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so one piece goes inside the other
strained means pulled out of shape, so the letters of priest are rearranged
the lid of a word is its first letter, here of casket

explanation.surface: A priest pulls a muscle lifting a coffin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strained' turns PRIEST into TRIEPS, which carries C.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: Bit of a step up for taxi drivers, vintage car ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of each of five words is taken

explanation.surface: An improvement for cab drivers: a classic car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'step up' seems to mean improvement, but the definition is part of a stair.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is the vertical board between two treads of a staircase.
